tldr: LLMs can self-improve through reinforcement learning using self-judging without ground truth answers, leveraging the generator-verifier gap where verifying solutions is computationally simpler than generating them. Qwen 2.5 7B DeepSeek Distilled trained with self-rewards achieved 75.5% accuracy on MIT Integration Bee problems, qualifying for the competition.
contributions: Demonstrated that LLMs can provide reliable reward signals for RL without ground truth answers by exploiting the generator-verifier asymmetry
Showed self-judging achieves performance comparable to formal verification across Countdown puzzles and integration problems
Established a complete self-improvement loop combining self-judging with synthetic question generation
Demonstrated Qwen 2.5 7B DeepSeek Distilled qualifies for the MIT Integration Bee (73% threshold) through pure self-supervised training
Showed periodic judge updates (every 50 steps) enable continued improvement beyond fixed-judge plateaus
methods: The authors use Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with batch size 64, rollout of 8, learning rate 1×10^-6, and KL loss coefficient 0.001. Models serve as both policy (generating solutions) and reward function (binary correct/incorrect judgment) without accessing ground truth. For integration problems, the self-judge prompt instructs the model to verify syntactic validity then apply symbolic differentiation to check if the derivative matches the original integrand. Experiments span three domains: Countdown arithmetic puzzles (2,000 training, 200 test), simple integration problems (2,000 training, 200 test synthetically generated by GPT-4o), and MIT Integration Bee problems augmented with 9,000 synthetic variants via the LADDER framework. Judge updates were tested at 50-step intervals versus fixed judges.
results: Qwen 2.5 7B achieved 96% verification accuracy vs 36% generation accuracy on Countdown (62 percentage point gap). For integration: Llama 3.2 3B achieved 47% verification vs 1% generation; Qwen 2.5 7B achieved 88% verification vs 46% generation; DeepSeek R1 achieved ~99% verification. Using Llama 3.2 3B as judge, the agent plateaued at ~48% test accuracy. Qwen 2.5 7B as judge enabled the agent to reach 75% after 150 training steps. DeepSeek R1 achieved performance comparable to symbolic verification (92% upper bound). Fixed judge plateaued at ~70% accuracy, while updated judge reached 75% (7% relative improvement) with verification accuracy improving from 88% to 93%. Continuous judge updates caused rapid training collapse. Qwen 2.5 7B DeepSeek Distilled crossed the 73% MIT Integration Bee qualification threshold at ~160 steps, reaching 75.5% by step 170.
limitations: Self-judging systems showed significant fragility requiring extensive iterative prompt design to prevent reward hacking. Less explicit prompts led to reward hacking with substantial drops in True Negative Rate. Early training improvements in integration tasks often reflected learning proper SymPy syntax rather than genuine mathematical reasoning gains. Continuous judge updates (every step) caused rapid training collapse due to feedback loops where poor solutions received high rewards. Performance eventually plateaus even with periodic updates, suggesting inherent limits to self-improvement through self-evaluation. Models failing to produce valid SymPy syntax are marked incorrect regardless of mathematical soundness, creating a confounding factor in evaluation.
